1: First day of the case. The Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) filed its criminal complaint and full investigation report against Adarsh Buildestate and others before the Gurugram Sessions Judge acting as Special Court under the Companies Act, with bulky records in four boxes. The court accepted it subject to checking and registration, told the court clerk (Ahlmad) to verify the documents and copies, and noted that besides those already arrested there are 178 more accused to be prosecuted. Adjourned to 24.5.2019 to consider summoning the other accused.
2: Copies of the complaint and full record were handed over to the lawyers for Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi; Vivek Harivyasi, who is on bail, will get his copy on 30.05.2019. The accused asked for a soft (electronic) copy because the record is huge; the SFIO investigating officer Prashant Baliyan said he would take instructions from his department. SFIO's arguments on summoning were partly heard and the case was adjourned to 28.05.2019.
3: Hearing on whether the court should take up the case and summon the accused. SFIO asked to file a corrected list of accused and witnesses with full addresses, explaining that although it seeks to prosecute about 186 accused, six names were accidentally left out of the original list. The court allowed the correction since it only fixes an inadvertent mistake in the title, and took the amended lists on record. More SFIO arguments were heard; next date 30.05.2019.
4: Vivek Harivyasi was excused from coming to court for the day because he suffered serious medical complications the night before and was admitted to Park Hospital, supported by medical records; he must appear on 01.07.2019. Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi, in jail, attended by video link and were kept in judicial custody till 13.06.2019. Arguments on summoning the accused finished; order fixed for 03.06.2019. The request for a soft copy of the complaint was refused because SFIO said none can be given.
5: Short order. A new lawyer, Ms. Shreya Dixit, filed her authority (power of attorney) for Vivek Harivyasi and received the copies of the complaint and the full record on his behalf, and her statement was recorded. The file was to be taken up after lunch the same day for the court's order on taking cognizance (formally taking up the case).
6: Short operative order summoning all 187 accused. Finding enough initial evidence, the court listed which companies and people face which charges: cheating and conspiracy, Companies Act fraud (Section 447), criminal breach of trust (Mukesh, Priyanka and Rahul Modi), forgery (the Modis, Vaibhav Lodha, Neha Gemawat, Jainam Rathod and others), illegally taking deposits, false accounts, and auditor offences (Abhay K Shah, S L Bohra & Associates). All are summoned through bailable warrants of Rs 10,000 to appear on 30.07.2019; SFIO must prepare the warrants within 15 days for service through the DCP Gurugram.
7: The detailed order taking up the SFIO complaint and summoning all 187 accused. It summarises the investigation: Mukesh Modi's Adarsh group took over Rs 1700 crore in loans from Adarsh Credit Cooperative Society (outstanding Rs 4120 crore), siphoned cash shown as cash in hand, used fake cloth-purchase bills and false deposit slips after demonetisation, a Noida land deal, the Riddhi Siddhi group, Vivek Harivyasi's companies and Riyasat Green Farm, auditor Abhay K Shah, Rajiv Kumar Rana and Mahesh Dutt Sharma. Finding enough initial evidence, the court framed the list of offences and issued bailable warrants of Rs 10,000 for 30.07.2019.
8: Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi were not brought from Gurugram jail because Rajasthan Police (Special Operations Group, Jaipur) had taken them to Jaipur in another case, FIR 24 of 2018, without this court's permission. The court issued a show-cause notice to the SOG station officer for not producing them and asked the Gurugram jail superintendent to explain handing them over. Production warrants were issued for the Modis for 17.06.2019 and, for several other accused already jailed in Jaipur, for 01.07.2019. Matter sent to the vacation judge S.K. Duggal.
9: Vacation judge order. SOG Jaipur Inspector Ravinder Kumar brought Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi to court, explaining they were on police remand in Jaipur till 22.6.2019 and could not be produced on 13.6.2019; he asked that they stay in police custody for the investigation. The Gurugram jail superintendent replied that no deliberate mistake was made in handing them over and regretted the inconvenience. The reply was kept for consideration on 1.7.2019, and the inspector was told to produce the accused that day.
10: Jaipur Police again failed to bring Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi, with no explanation; a police official said other accused could not be brought for lack of police force. Fresh production warrants were issued for the Modis and others (Ishwar Singh Sindal, Bharat Modi, Vaibhav Lodha, Bharat Das Vaishnav, Rohit Modi, Virender Modi, Vivek Purohit) for 30.07.2019. Priyanka Modi, produced in custody, was kept in judicial custody till 15.07.2019. Vivek Harivyasi applied for bail on the added offences while SFIO asked to cancel his existing bail; his bail was extended till the hearing on 05.07.2019.
11: Short remand order. Priyanka Modi, who was in custody, was brought to court by the jail authorities. SFIO's team (senior standing counsel Lokender Raghav, prosecutor Hari Kishan and investigating officer Prashant Baliyan) asked for her further custody. The court agreed and kept her in judicial custody till 30.07.2019, directing that she be produced again on that date through video conferencing.
12: First appearance date after summoning, dealing with each of the 187 accused. Group companies are to be represented by Rohit Modi, Sidharth Chauhan, Vivek Harivyasi, Surender Singh and others. Many warrants came back unserved and were reissued for 04.09.19 with the complaint. Requests by Paras Bolia, the Tak family, Peeyush Aggarwal and others to be excused from coming to court on medical or personal grounds were rejected as afterthoughts. Jainam Rathod, Raj Kumar Modi, Ramlal Arya and others surrendered and were let out on interim bail of Rs 50,000 and had to deposit passports. Auditors Ichchhita Dungarwal and Neha Kataria got bail because their offences are bailable.
13: Rohit Modi was brought from custody and marked present for the Adarsh group companies. Bail hearings for Surender Singh, Jainam Rathod, Raj Kumar Modi and ten accused directors who say they signed the account books without bad intent were put off to 20.8.2019, with interim bail extended. Bharat Kumar Mardia argued he was not summoned for fraud under Section 447. Raj Kumar Modi was excused from coming that day because he was unwell. The Modis and Vivek Harivyasi stayed in judicial custody, and Vaibhav Lodha, Virender Modi, Rohit Modi and others already held in Jaipur were also taken into custody in this case.
14: Only Vivek Harivyasi was brought (from Bhondsi jail, Gurugram) and was kept in judicial custody till 04.09.2019, to appear by video link. The other ten accused held in Central Jail, Jaipur, including Mukesh Modi, Rahul Modi and Priyanka Modi, were not produced and the jail sent no information; SFIO's counsel said Rahul and Mukesh Modi had perhaps been taken by Gujarat police. Fresh production warrants were issued for 4.9.2019 and the Jaipur jail superintendent was asked to explain why they were not produced.
15: Bail refused. By a separate detailed order, the court dismissed the regular bail applications of Jainam Rathod, Surender Singh, Ajit Singh Rathore, Ram Lal Arya, Hemant Kumar Jain, Praveen Kumar, Damyanti Bhandari, Nimesh Kumar Soni, Rituraj Singh Sisodia, Dushyant Singh Rathore, Shashank Shekhar Singh Rathore and Jitesh Kumar Parmar, who were present in court; they were taken into custody and sent to Bhondsi jail, Gurugram, till 4.9.2019. Bharat Kumar Mardia's application for anticipatory bail (protection from arrest) was also dismissed and an arrest warrant issued against him for 4.9.2019.
16: Raj Kumar Modi's regular bail application was dismissed by a separate detailed order and his interim bail from 13.8.2019 was cancelled. He did not come to court even though he was on interim bail and supposed to appear, and his lawyer gave no explanation. An arrest warrant was issued for 04.09.2019, his bail and surety bonds were forfeited, and his surety was given a notice to explain why action should not be taken for his non-appearance.
17: Long roll-call order. Jaipur jail again failed to bring Rohit Modi, Mukesh Modi, Rahul Modi and others; new production warrants and an explanation were ordered. Sidharth Chauhan, refused anticipatory bail on 1.8.2019, still had not surrendered; arrest warrant sent to the DCP. Raj Kumar Modi stayed absent; notice went to his surety Rekha Modi. Rajeev Verma, Sushil Maloo and Rajendra Singh Bhandari were excused from attending. Abhay K Shah, the Tak family and others got protection from arrest until their anticipatory bail is decided. Arrest warrants were issued against accused found deliberately avoiding service, such as Peeyush Aggarwal and Paras Bolia. Vijay Shukla showed a Supreme Court no-coercive-action order.
18: Short order about Vijay Shukla (A-149), who appeared in person. He filed a copy of the Supreme Court's order of the same day adjourning his writ petition to 12.9.2019 and continuing the interim protection that no coercive action (such as arrest) be taken against him. He was directed to appear in this court on 13.9.2019, subject to the Supreme Court's further directions.
19: Vijay Shukla showed that the Supreme Court had adjourned his case to 19.9.2019 and extended his protection from arrest, so he must appear on 20.9.2019. Separately, the anticipatory bail applications of Shinder Pal Singh and Gurbir Singh Sandhu were dismissed by a detailed order, their temporary protection was withdrawn, and arrest warrants were issued for 03.10.2019 through a special police team with SFIO officials. The landlord of Shinder Pal Singh's rented house in Sector 9-B, Chandigarh had complained that police were deliberately not arresting him, so that address goes on the warrant.
20: Paramvir Singh Sangwan (A-174) asked that his arrest warrant be put on hold because the High Court, in his writ petition (CWP 23904 of 2019), had passed an interim order on 13.09.2019 in the same terms as the Supreme Court's no-coercive-action order for Vijay Shukla. The court accepted this and directed that the arrest warrant issued on 04.09.2019 not be carried out, informing the DCP (HQ) Gurugram. Notice of his application went to SFIO for 27.09.2019.
21: Roll-call order. Central Jail Jaipur again did not send Rohit Modi and nine other jailed accused, claiming a Jaipur magistrate (ACMM) needed them; the court found this baseless, since the ACMM never barred sending them and has no power over this Special Court. Fresh production warrants were issued for 03.10.2019, with copies to the ACMM and the Jaipur SSP to provide police escort. Mukesh Modi, Rahul Modi and Ishwar Singh Sindal were said to be with Ahmedabad police. Arrest warrants were renewed for Sidharth Chauhan and Raj Kumar Modi. Six accused had been granted anticipatory bail (protection from arrest); custody of others extended.
22: Joydeep Das Gupta, Lovekush Sharma, Poonam Madan, Praveen Maheshwari, Rajeev Maheshwari and Avanish Kumar Tyagi, who had been granted anticipatory bail, furnished their bail bonds. The five who work as senior executives asked to be freed from depositing their passports since they must travel often. SFIO's counsel did not dispute that it is basically a case of no evidence against these six, so the court dropped the conditions to hand over passports and not to leave India without permission. Avanish Kumar Tyagi swore an affidavit that he has no passport. All to appear 3.10.2019.
23: Hearing on Vivek Harivyasi's bail, with him present on bail and senior counsel Satish Aggarwal for SFIO. After some argument, both sides relied on new facts and case law against each other and asked for time to study the judgments cited. The case was adjourned to 17.07.2019 for further arguments, and Vivek Harivyasi's existing bail was extended till then on the same terms.
24: Correction order, pronounced 11 July 2019. SFIO pointed out copy-paste (clerical) mistakes in the list of who was summoned for what in the 03.06.2019 summoning order: names of individual accused A-115 to A-141 were missing from the fraud paragraph, company names were missing elsewhere, Virender Modi was left out, Bharat Mardia was wrongly written instead of Bharat Modi, and Shinder Pal Singh, Gurbir Singh Sandhu and Mahesh Dutt Sharma were wrongly included in one paragraph. Relying on a Supreme Court ruling on clerical errors, the court allowed the correction and replaced paragraph 9 with a corrected list.
25: Anticipatory bail (protection from arrest) hearings for twelve accused including Jinendra Vyas, auditor Abhay K Shah, the Tak family, Megha Chauhan, Shyam Bihari Gupta, Sudhir Mehta, Raj Kumar Bohra and Mahesh Dutt Sharma. After two hours of argument for Vyas and Shah, all twelve were adjourned to 23.9.2019 because Mahendra Tak's senior lawyer R.K. Handoo had to go to Ludhiana; their temporary protection was extended. Nitin Rathore's request to cancel his arrest warrant without surrendering, claiming he had moved address 5-6 years ago, was dismissed as a delaying tactic.
26: Vijay Shukla (A-149) appeared and filed the Supreme Court's order of 19.09.2019: his request for interim relief was turned down, but he was allowed to seek anticipatory or regular bail in the proper court, and his protection from arrest was extended for ten days to do so. He had not filed any bail application yet, so he was left free to do so within that time. Next date 03.10.2019.
27: Short adjournment. The case was listed for the court's decision on the anticipatory bail (protection from arrest) applications of auditor Abhay K Shah (CIS No. 3303 of 2019) and Jinender Vyas (CIS No. 3320 of 2019), with their local lawyers present, but the orders were not ready. Put off to 23.9.2019 for orders on both applications.
28: Part arguments heard on anticipatory bail (protection from arrest) applications of the Tak family (Mahesh Kumar, Saurabh, Ravi, Indu, Mahendra Kumar Tak), Raj Kumar Bohra, Sudhir Mehta, Shyam Bihari Gupta, Megha Chauhan, Mahesh Dutt Sharma, Paras Bolia and Shiv Raj Sharma; further hearing on 30.9.2019 since a similar case was pending in the High Court. After lunch, auditor Abhay K Shah's anticipatory bail was dismissed by a detailed order, his temporary protection withdrawn, and, as he had not surrendered, an arrest warrant was issued for 03.10.2019.
29: Jinender (Jinendra) Vyas's anticipatory bail application (protection from arrest) was dismissed by a separate detailed order, and his temporary protection was withdrawn. Because he had not surrendered, an arrest warrant was issued against him for 03.10.2019. The file was also listed for 27.9.2019 on Paramvir Singh Sangwan's request to withdraw his arrest warrant.
30: Paramvir Singh Sangwan's request to withdraw his arrest warrant. His lawyer said the Punjab and Haryana High Court had on 26.9.2019 listed his writ petition for a later date and told this court to decide his bail on merits, though the certified copy had not arrived. Since he has now applied for anticipatory bail, to be heard with similar accused, the court ordered that his arrest warrant not be carried out till 04.10.2019, subject to any High Court directions.
31: Remand order by Additional Sessions Judge A.K. Bishnoi, as the regular judge was on casual leave. Vivek Harivyasi attended through video conferencing. Jainam Rathod, Ajit Singh Rathore, Ram Lal Arya, Hemant Kumar Jain, Praveen Kumar, Damyanti Bhandari, Nimesh Kumar Soni, Rituraj Singh, Dushyant Singh Rathore, Shashank Shekhar Singh Rathore, Jitesh Kumar Parmar, Surender Singh and Priyanka Modi were produced in custody. All were kept in judicial custody till 14.10.2019, to be produced by video conferencing.
32: New Sessions Judge M.M. Dhonchak handled many requests to be excused from coming to court. Aditya Sarda was excused for the day despite an arrest warrant, citing viral fever without a medical certificate; the Maheshwari brothers (out of station on work) and several company representatives (fever, out of station) were also excused for the day. Abhay K Shah's request was refused as his anticipatory bail was already dismissed, and Vimal Sanwarmal Sharma's was refused as the High Court gave him no protection. Vijay Shukla was excused while his anticipatory bail is pending. Non-bailable warrants against Sidharth Chauhan, Peeyush Aggarwal and others were reissued; the Modis came from custody.
33: Short procedural order by Sessions Judge M.M. Dhonchak. Lawyers appeared for many accused with pending bail applications, including Paramvir Singh Sangwan, the Tak family, Shyam Bihari Gupta, Sudhir Mehta, Raj Kumar Bohra, Megha Chauhan, Vijay Shukla, Mahesh Dutt Sharma, Naveen Choudhary, Paras Bolia, Nitin Rathore and Shiv Raj Sharma. The court said separate orders had been passed on the bail applications and need not be repeated. Next date 14.10.2019.
34: Routine custody date. Vivek Harivyasi, Jainam Rathod, Ajit Singh Rathore, Ram Lal Arya, Hemant Kumar Jain, Praveen Kumar, Damyanti Bhandari, Nimesh Kumar Soni, Rituraj Singh, Dushyant Singh Rathore, Shashank Shekhar Singh Rathore, Jitesh Kumar Parmar and Surender Singh were marked present by video conferencing, and Priyanka Modi was brought to court. All are to be produced before the court on 19.10.2019.
35: Roll-call order by Additional Sessions Judge Raj Gupta. Jaipur jail did not bring Rohit Modi, citing too few police, nor the Modis and Priyanka Modi; Bhondsi jail did not bring Vivek Harivyasi, Surender Singh, Jainam Rathod and others, so all were summoned for 2.11.2019. Abhay K Shah's request to be excused while he approaches the High Court was refused. People excused for the day on medical grounds: Praveen and Rajeev Maheshwari (lung infection/bronchitis), Aditya Sarda (viral fever, chest pain), a company representative (diarrhoea). Bharat Kumar Mardia was excused as the High Court extended his pre-arrest bail. Arrest warrants against Jinendra Vyas, Shinder Pal Singh and others were extended.
36: Roll-call order by Judge Raj Gupta. Rohit Modi, Mukesh Modi, Rahul Modi, Priyanka Modi and others were finally brought from Jaipur jail, and Vivek Harivyasi, Surender Singh and Jainam Rathod from Bhondsi, all kept in custody till 22.11.2019. Abhay K Shah's request to be excused was refused as the High Court gave no interim protection. Bharat Kumar Mardia was let out on bail of Rs 50,000 under the High Court's pre-arrest bail order. Excused for the day: Poonam Madan (work at DLF), Praveen Maheshwari (meeting in Chennai for Wheels India), Aditya Sarda (documents not supplied), Vimal Sanwarmal Sharma (viral fever) and Ichchhita Dungarwal (two-year-old child unwell).
37: Pure adjournment. No one appeared; the file was taken up early because 11.11.2019 had been declared a local holiday, and the case was adjourned to a later date (left blank in the order) for the same purpose, with all concerned to be informed. Order by Additional Sessions Judge Raj Gupta.
38: Roll-call order by Judge Raj Gupta. Vivek Harivyasi was not produced as he had been taken to the government hospital, Gurugram, for ill-health. The High Court had refused bail to Sidharth Chauhan, Surender Singh, Jainam Rathod and Raj Kumar Modi. A police constable's salary was ordered attached for falsely reporting that Abhay K Shah was away on a religious trip. Damyanti Bhandari, now on bail, applied to become an approver (witness for the prosecution) under a High Court order; Nimesh Soni and Shashank Shekhar Singh Rathore had similar applications. Joydeep Das Gupta, Poonam Madan, Ichchhita Dungarwal and others were excused from appearing until further orders.
39: Roll-call order by Judge Raj Gupta, mostly by video link; next date 31.1.2020. Rahul Modi, Mukesh Modi and Ishwar Singh Sindal were not produced as they had been taken to courts in Junagarh and Sabarmati. Abhay K Shah and Nitin Rathore were refused excuse from attending as the High Court had given them no protection. Aditya Sarda's request to cancel his arrest warrant was refused; he had been deliberately avoiding service. Rajiv Kumar Rana got temporary protection from arrest pending anticipatory bail. Ajit Singh Rathore, Ramlal Arya, Damyanti Bhandari and other bailed accused are to give statements as approvers (prosecution witnesses) as the High Court directed.
40: Roll-call order by new judge Dr. D.N. Bhardwaj; next date 08.05.2020. Rohit Modi, the Modis, Priyanka Modi, Vivek Harivyasi, Jainam Rathod, Surender Singh and Raj Kumar Modi appeared from jail by video link. Abhay K Shah and Nitin Rathore were refused excuse from coming, as no High Court order protected them. Jai Singh Chauhan, representative of the Riddhi Siddhi companies, was excused for the day for a family wedding. Bharat Kumar Mardia and the Maheshwari brothers were excused until further orders because they live and do business in different parts of India. Fresh arrest warrants went out for Sidharth Chauhan, Jinendra Vyas, Shinder Pal Singh and Gurbir Singh Sandhu.
41: Pure adjournment due to COVID-19. No one appeared. The file was taken up early under an order (Endst. No. 2495 dated 02.05.2020) of the District and Sessions Judge, Gurugram, issued because of the situation arising from the coronavirus (COVID-19) outbreak. The case was adjourned to 24.09.2020 for the same purpose already fixed, and all concerned were to be informed.
42: COVID-19 period hearing fixed for presence of accused; most did not appear, and the case was adjourned to 14.01.2021, with warrants to continue against those without bail or protection. Jailed accused were not produced because video conferencing was not working. Many were excused from attending, including company representatives, Paramvir Singh Sangwan, Leena and Vivek Harivyasi, and the Tak family. Vijay Jindal's request, saying he was being admitted to AIIMS Delhi for treatment, was refused since his anticipatory bail was rejected and the High Court gave no protection. Mahesh Dutt Sharma's High Court protection was extended to 3.11.2020; Vimal Sanwarmal Sharma furnished bail bonds.
43: Short order by Additional Sessions Judge Dr. D.N. Bhardwaj. The file was taken up on the application of accused Raj Kumar Bohra, through his advocate B.S. Motsara, for furnishing bail. His bail bonds and surety bonds were furnished as required by the earlier order dated 11.08.2020 and accepted; after compliance the papers were to be attached to the main case file.
44: Pure adjournment due to COVID-19. No one appeared. The file was taken up under an order (Endst. No. 01 dated 02.01.2021) of the District and Sessions Judge, Gurugram, issued because of the coronavirus (COVID-19) situation. The case was adjourned to 15.01.2021 for the same purpose already fixed, and all concerned were to be informed of the new date.
45: Hearing for presence of accused. Mahesh Kumar Tak (A-187) was reported to have died. Company representatives, Megha Chauhan, Indu Tak, Ravi Tak and Jitesh Kumar Parmar were excused from attending, but Vijay Shukla's request (gone to Chandigarh for his anticipatory bail in the High Court) was refused since he had no protection. Jailed accused, including the Modis, Rohit Modi and Jainam Rathod, were not produced because video conferencing was not connected. Surender Singh was still in Virat Hospital, Rewari, and his lawyer must file his medical records. Approver applications of Ajit Singh Rathore, Ram Lal Arya and others are pending; their statements to be recorded 19.02.2021.
46: The jailed accused (Rohit Modi, Mukesh Modi, Rahul Modi, Priyanka Modi, Jainam Rathod and others) were again not produced because video conferencing was not connected; SFIO's officers joined by WhatsApp. For Surender Singh, who is in hospital, only a medical certificate was filed without treatment records, and his lawyer sought time as his senior was unavailable. The court directed Dr. Virender Yadav or the in-charge of Virat Hospital, Rewari, to produce his treatment record in court through a knowledgeable person by 19.1.2021.
47: Only Jainam Rathod and Raj Kumar Modi were produced from custody by video link; the other jailed accused were not. For Surender Singh, Sandeep, in charge of nursing staff at Virat Hospital, Rewari, produced only an ICU chart from 11.1.2021 and blood reports of 16-18.1.2021 and could not explain his medical condition. He said the treating doctor, who could not join by video, would come with the full record. SFIO did not object, and the case was adjourned to 21.01.2021 for the treating doctor to appear with complete medical records.
48: Dr. Viratveer Yadav of Virat Hospital, Rewari appeared by video and said Surender Singh had COVID-19 and is now on intermittent BiPAP support (a breathing machine) with chest physiotherapy for severe lung fibrosis caused by the coronavirus, but is recovering well and can be moved in 10-15 days. His treatment records did not arrive because hospital staff were stuck in a traffic jam near village Masani due to the farmers' protest (Kisan Andolan). The court ordered him shifted back to Bhondsi jail on 1.2.2021 and allowed SFIO to have a Medical Board verify his condition and treatment.
49: Only Jainam Rathod and Surender Singh were produced from custody by video link; the others were not as the video link was not connected, and Raj Kumar Modi was said to be in Civil Hospital, Gurugram. The court corrected the 15.1.2021 order to record that Shashank Shekhar Singh Rathore, Nimesh Kumar Soni and Damyanti Bhandari had in fact been present. Vijay Shukla filed a High Court order of 28.1.2021 (CRM 24870 of 2020) barring coercive action against him, so no action is to be taken against him on the non-bailable warrant.
50: Hearing for presence of accused. Mahendra Kumar Tak (A-155) was reported dead, in addition to Mahesh Kumar Tak (A-187); death reports were called from police. Padmawati Art Creation appeared through its representative Fateh Singh. Paramvir Singh Sangwan, aged 74 with old-age illnesses and at high COVID-19 risk, was excused from attending until further orders. Vijay Shukla keeps High Court protection. The Modis and others were not produced because Rajasthan Police had taken them on police remand. Statements of accused who want to become approvers (witnesses for the prosecution), such as Ajit Singh Rathore, Ram Lal Arya and Damyanti Bhandari, were scheduled from 5.3.2021 to 30.4.2021.
